gloss: great blessing; very lucky; best fortune

definitions.gloss: great blessing; excellent fortune; best luck
definitions.explanation: The highest rank of fortune on an omikuji (fortune slip) drawn at a shrine or temple. By extension, used to describe something extremely lucky or auspicious.

examples.japanese: おみくじで{大吉|だいきち}が{出|で}た！
examples.english: I drew the best fortune on my omikuji!

examples.japanese: {初詣|はつもうで}で{大吉|だいきち}を{引|ひ}いて、{幸先|さいさき}がいい。
examples.english: I drew the best fortune at the New Year shrine visit — a good omen.

examples.japanese: {三年|さんねん}{連続|れんぞく}で{大吉|だいきち}を{引|ひ}いたので、{今年|ことし}もいい{年|とし}になりそうだ。
examples.english: I've drawn the best fortune three years in a row, so this year looks like it will be a good one too.

notes:
The highest-ranked fortune on an おみくじ (fortune slip) drawn at shrines and temples. {大|だい} means 'great' and {吉|きち} means 'good fortune.'

OMIKUJI FORTUNE RANKINGS (from best to worst):
- {大吉|だいきち} — great blessing
- {吉|きち} — blessing
- {中吉|ちゅうきち} — moderate blessing
- {小吉|しょうきち} — small blessing
- {末吉|すえきち} — near-blessing
- {凶|きょう} — bad luck
- {大凶|だいきょう} — terrible luck

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大吉|だいきち}を{引|ひ}く — to draw the best fortune
- {大吉|だいきち}が{出|で}る — to get the best fortune
- おみくじで{大吉|だいきち} — best fortune on an omikuji

CULTURAL NOTE:
Drawing おみくじ is a popular custom at {初詣|はつもうで} (first shrine visit of the year). Getting {大吉|だいきち} is considered very auspicious. Some people tie bad fortune slips to a tree at the shrine to leave the bad luck behind, while keeping {大吉|だいきち} slips.
